newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - June 25.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - June 25.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing,
Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:
HONG KONG - Hong Kong lawmakers have passed a tough law
banning tobacco advertisements in the press and in public
places, including the display of cigarette brands at sports and
cultural events. In Sri Lanka, the government says it plans to
cut tobacco and alcohol promotion.
BONN - Germany's advertising industry fears that increasing
regulatory pressure on tobacco manufacturers will lead to more
restrictions on tobacco advertising. The ZAW German Federation
of Advertisers says tobacco companies should continue to have
the right to advertise and that existing legal and
self-regulatory restrictions are tight enough.
SINGAPORE - Foote Cone & Belding, the U.S.-based advertising
agency, announces acquisition of Lloyd Martin, an ad agency in
Singapore with billings of Singapore $12 million. At the
International Advertising Festival in Cannes, an FCB executive
says FCB is in a stronger position to win global accounts since
its parent company, True North Communications, ended its
alliance with France's Publicis this year.
CHICAGO - FCB's parent, True North Communications, is in
talks to acquire rival advertising agency New York-based Bozell,
Jacobs, Kenyon & Eckhardt in a stock swap valued at more than
$375 million, sources close to the talks say.
CANNES - Three Scandinavian advertising agencies owned by
Interpublic's McCann-Erickson network say they have formed a
joint venture to focus on the pan-European advertising market.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:
LE MANS, France - French telephone operator France Telecom
says it's working on a simplified terminal for Internet access
with several European and North American companies. Wanadoo, France Telecom's Internet service provider, plans a major
promotion in the autumn to boost market share. Wanadoo has
43,000 subscribers.
WASHINGTON - American Television executives are close to an
agreement with parent groups on revamping the TV industry's
programme ratings system to include references for violence, sex
and strong language, a U.S. senator says.
REDMOND - Microsoft Corp executives say they expect to spend
$1.5 billion on developing Internet-related software in the
financial year that ends on June 30, 1998.
MUNICH - TV-shopping channel H.O.T. is to add a further
560,000 cable households to its coverage from July by gaining a
licence in the southern German state of Baden-Wuerttemberg. The
licence means some 9.4 million households in Germany and Austria
can receive the channel.
PARIS - French pay television firm Canal Plus plans to swap
its 37.5 percent interest in German pay TV channel Premiere for
a 45 percent stake in Italy's Telepieu held by Bavarian media
mogul Leo Kirch, the French daily La Tribune says.
HAMBURG - Should Kirch and Bertelsmann-affiliate CLT-Ufa run
into cartel problems with their planned cooperation, they appear
to have won some political backing for their cause. Wolfgang
Clement, Economics Minister in the German state of North
Rhine-Westphalia, says recent federal cartel office criticism of
the deal is premature.
LONDON - Britain's Granada Group Plc says it's making an
agreed bid to take over Yorkshire-Tyne Tees Television Holdings
Plc in a move valuing Yorkshire at 711 million pounds ($1.2
billion).
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:
LONDON - Animal welfare groups and retailers including
Tesco, Sainsbury and the Body Shop join forces to launch their
own international standard to guarantee against testing
cosmetics on animals.
LOS ANGELES - Nike Inc apologises to the Islamic community
as it recalls more than 38,000 pairs of athletic shoes with a
logo that offended Muslims because it resembled the Arabic word
for "Allah", or God.
HAMBURG - Tobacco group Reemtsma hopes to maintain its
growth rates with acquisitions in Eastern Europe and Asia.
Management board chairman Ludger Staby says the group is already
the world's fastest growing cigarette producer and is targeting
10 percent sales growth for the current year. Sales target for
1997 is 120 billion cigarettes, he says
NEW DELHI - B.A.T Industries Plc's premium cigarette brands
which are due to be launched in India will enter a stagnant
market with low consumption levels that offers challenges but
also good opportunities, a top industry official says.
DETROIT - U.S. carmakers are going to take a hard look at
prices for the forthcoming 1998 model year. They are expected to
offer a variety of modest price hikes, outright price cuts and enhanced equipment packages for no extra cost to lure people
into showrooms, industry analysts say.
PARIS - PSA Peugeot Citroen revises downward its market
forecast, saying it expects French car sales to fall by 15.6
percent in 1997 from a year earlier to 1.80 million
registrations.
BRUSSELS - Sales of Daimler-Benz AG cars climbed 11 percent
in the first five months of 1997 to more than 20.4 billion marks
($11.8 billion), a senior executive says.
FRANKFURT - Eurocheques are facing an uncertain future as
one of Germany's most popular and well-known means of paying for
medium-sized transactions. Research shows a steady decline in
usage of Eurocheques in favour of cash and credit cards.
TOKYO - Fuji Photo Film co, the Japanese photographic film
maker, says it is not engaged in a price war with its biggest
rival Eastman Kodak Co in the U.S. photo film market. Concerns
that Kodak is facing pressure over prices from Fuji Photo have
recently hit Kodak's share price in the U.S..
LONDON - The share price of Dixons, the British electrical
retailer, slipped after a press report said Tesco, the
supermarket group, was planning to start selling television sets
in its stores.
CONSUMER TRENDS:
PARIS - French teenagers are getting a taste of wine, beer
and spirits at a younger age than they did a decade ago in a
country with one of the world's highest rates of alcohol
consumption, according to a survey by the Institute of
Scientific Research on Drink.
RIO DE JANEIRO - Brazil's hot little beach numbers, the
world-famous "dental floss" bikinis, are looking to grow -- not
in size but in popularity. Their makers are looking to export
the tiny garments when the summer season in Latin America fades
and bikini sales slump, say industry experts.
AMSTERDAM - Drugs companies are racing to find the best
treatment for migraine, which affects 585 million people -- one
in 10 of the world's population, say industry experts.
GENEVA - The Swiss have the highest proportion of computer
users along with the U.S. and Denmark, while Finland has the
highest proportion of "surfers" on the Internet computer
network. More couples stay in wedlock in the Mediterranean
countries of Italy, Turkey and Greece while the rate of divorce
is highest in Estonia, Latvia, Belgium, Sweden, Finland, Russia
and Britain. These snippets of information are revealed in the
latest annual United Nations reference book.
LONDON - British women who wait until they are in their 30s
to have babies now outnumber those who start families in their
early 20s, the government says.
ZOLTIKOVSKY, Russia - Russian consumers still clamour for
fur despite the cost. Most women own at least one fur coat. The
basic type is an astrakhan. Mink is considered expensive. Sable
is even dearer and seen as a must for every wife or girlfriend
of a newly-rich Russian, say industry experts.
WARSAW - The number of Poles who drink beer has risen by six
percent over the past year, a survey by Pentor research group
shows.
